chunks: And Al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Sayābah narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

The testimony of the player of nard, the player of al-arbaʿata ʿashar, and the player of chess is not accepted. He says, ‘No, by Allah,’ and ‘Yes, by Allah,’ and ‘By Allah, his king died,’ and ‘By Allah, his king was killed,’ while Allah, exalted is His mention, is his King; He neither died nor was killed.

key_terms.الْأَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ: a named game mentioned here among discredited forms of play
key_terms.شَاهُهُ: his king, referring to the king piece in the game
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: legal testimony given in a judicial or probative context
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الشَّاهَيْنِ: the player of chess, literally the one associated with the two shahs

ai.seo_question: Why is the testimony of players of nard and chess rejected in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that the testimony of those known for playing certain games such as nard, al-arbaʿata ʿashar, and chess is not accepted. It also condemns their casual and improper use of oaths and expressions about the ‘king’ piece, contrasting that with Allah, exalted is His mention, Who neither dies nor is killed.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3291 - And Al-'Ala ibn Sayabah narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"The testimony of the player of nard (a type of board game), the one who plays arba'ata 'ashar (a gambling game), and the player of chess is not accepted. They say, 'No, by Allah (swt),' and 'Yes, by Allah (swt),' and 'By Allah (swt), his king (chess piece) died,' and 'By Allah (swt), his king (chess piece) was killed,' while Allah (swt), exalted is His mention, is the true King who neither dies nor is killed."
